messages:
emily: Hey all, first week here. Running `docker-compose up` but our app errors on startup: `ERROR: relation "spatial_ref_sys" does not exist` — looks like PostGIS missing. I dropped an `init-postgis.sql` into ./db/init and mounted it to /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d but it never ran. Any tips?

diego: welcome! two quick things: 1) the entrypoint scripts only run if the postgres data dir is empty (first init). if you previously started the container with a host mount it may have data, so scripts are skipped. 2) file ownership/permissions can block the entrypoint from reading files.

emily: ah, I do have ./db/data mounted. The compose snippet is:
```
services:
  db:
    image: postgis/postgis:14-3.3
    volumes:
      - ./db/data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
```

tara: yep, since the data dir already had files, init scripts won't run. Easiest repro path: `docker-compose down -v` to remove volumes (host bind stays but named volumes removed) or temporarily use a named volume for fresh init: `- db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data` then `docker-compose up`.

diego: also check that your `init` scripts are plain SQL or executable shell scripts and owned by root (or readable by postgres). sometimes editors add \r or weird perms. do `ls -l ./db/init` and `file ./db/init/init-postgis.sql` to verify.

emily: `ls -l` shows `-rw-r--r-- 1 emily staff 2048 Apr 1 10:00 init-postgis.sql`. I tried `docker-compose down -v` but since I have a host bind for ./db/data the folder still has files.

tara: right, host bind is persistent. Two options: 1) remove ./db/data contents (backup first) and then `docker-compose up` to trigger init, or 2) start a throwaway container with named volume, let it run the init, then switch the app to that volume. For local dev we usually recommend a named volume to avoid host-perm headaches.

emily: I copied the SQL into a running container and ran it manually with `docker-compose exec db psql -U postgres -f /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-postgis.sql` and now the app starts. Is that okay or should I re-init?

diego: manual apply is fine for dev. Just know the entrypoint path is handy for first-run automation. If you want a clean workflow: delete the host data dir (or move it), use named volume, confirm PostGIS installed by the image, and keep init scripts in ./db/init.

devex-bot: devex note: checklist for init scripts: 1) mount path correct 2) DB data dir empty for entrypoint to run 3) script permissions readable in container 4) use named volumes to avoid host permission issues. Internal guide: https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-init

emily: thanks everyone! I documented the manual psql workaround in my onboarding notes and will switch to a named volume for future runs. Appreciate the help :)
